names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 30 Δεκεμβρίου, «Άγιος Γεδεών ο Νέος Οσιομάρτυρας», with the rank and the by-name left off. The page also gives his name in the world, «κατά κόσμον ονομαζόταν Νικόλαος», and the Muslim name he was given under duress, Ιμπραήμ; both are recorded in the life and neither is stored as a form of his monastic name.

Read out of the Охридски пролог's fifth heading for 30. децембар ст. ст., „Преподобни мученик Гедеон.“ — «Преподобни мученик» is the `venerable-martyr` the folder already carries, and the heading gives no by-name, no see and no place, so §6 leaves the bare forename. Measured before it was written: `fk.mjs` returns no other holder of this string or of anything folding to it.

death.note: saint.gr: «παρέδωσε το πνεύμα του στις 30 Δεκεμβρίου 1818 μ.Χ.», with the page's own head «(; - 1818)». No year of birth is given; the page dates one episode of his life, his appointment to the metochion, to 6 June 1797.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 30ης Δεκεμβρίου — «Άγιος Γεδεών ο Νέος Οσιομάρτυρας»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 30 Δεκεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and that day is also the day of his death, which the page dates to the year. The corpus holds only `gideon-the-righteous` for this name, who is the judge of Israel, so there is nothing here for this man to be confused with. `types` carries `venerable-martyr` for the page's own Οσιομάρτυρας, `new-martyr` for its Νέος and for the date, and `monk` for the tonsure at Karakallou. It names his village Κάπουρνα of Demetrias in the prefecture of Magnesia, his parents Αυγερινός and Κυράτζα, three brothers and four sisters, the villages Γιερμή, Βελεστίνο and Κεραμίδι, Crete, the monastery of Karakallou on the Holy Mountain, the metochion of the Transfiguration in the region of Rethymno, the former abbot Γαβριήλ with whom he was appointed to it on 6 June 1797, Αγιά where he was arrested, and Τύρναβος where he died; the corpus holds no folder this reading could attach to any of the persons, and no coordinate is proposed for any of the places. It names Tyrnavos as the town that holds him patron and two places of his relic, his skull in the metropolitan church of the Panagia Phaneromeni at Tyrnavos and a part at Karakallou. It prints two apolytikia, both of which name him and both of which are taken; the second is marked «Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον». No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 12.01.2026 (30. децембар ст. ст.) — „Преподобни мученик Гедеон.“

attestations.note: The day's fifth entry. The identification is the Athonite monastery, the denial, the manner of death and the year together: Karakallou, the fingers and toes cut off, the latrine, and 1818, all of which the folder's own life already tells out of saint.gr, and the Greek keeps him on this same menologion day. The serbian row was `undocumented`, so the row lands here. `dates` UNTOUCHED AND AGREEING EXACTLY: the entry gives «1818. године» and the folder holds a flat 1818. `types` UNTOUCHED: «Преподобни мученик» is the `venerable-martyr` held. NO `locations`: SEE THE LIFE — THE TWO BOOKS DISAGREE ABOUT WHERE HE DIED, saint.gr putting it at Tyrnavos in Thessaly and this book «у месту Турнову у Тракији», at a place Turnovo in Thrace, and both readings are now in the life and neither is chosen between. NO `related`: «светом Јакову Персијанцу (в. 27. новембар)» is named only as the likeness of a torture and a comparison is not a companion, so the name stays in the book's own Cyrillic and NO ROW WAS PUT ON `james-the-persian` IN EITHER DIRECTION; the spiritual father who gave him the blessing is unnamed. WHAT THE BOOK ADDS: that he was a Greek by descent and of very poor parents; that he was made a Turk by force in his youth; that he repented and fled to the Holy Mountain and took the monastic habit at Karakallou; that he took his spiritual father's blessing before he went, and that he reviled Mohammed openly before the Turks as a false prophet, which no source this folder had said; that they shaved his head and set him backwards on a donkey and led him through the town, AND THAT HE REJOICED IN THAT MOCKERY FOR CHRIST'S SAKE; and that his wonderworking relics rest in the church of the Holy Apostles in the village of Turnovo with a part of them at Karakallou, where saint.gr had his head in the metropolitan church of Tyrnavos. The Prologue prints no hymn (8 October 2026).

hymns.text: Ἐναθλήσας νομίμως τὸν ἐχθρὸν καταβέβληκας, καὶ Ὁσιομάρτυς ἐδείχθης, του Σωτῆρος περίδοξος· χειρῶν γὰρ καὶ ποδῶν τὴν ἐκτομήν, ὑπέστης Γεδεὼν καρτερικῶς, διὰ τοῦτο θείαν χάριν νέμεις ἀεί, τοῖς πίστει ἐκβοῶσί σοι· δόξα τῷ παρασχόντι σοι ἰσχύν, δόξα τῷ σὲ στεφανώσαντι, δόξα τῷ ἐνεργοῦντι διὰ σοῦ, πᾶσιν ἰάματα.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος α´, Τῆς ἐρήμου πολίτης — the first of two apolytikia on the page of «Άγιος Γεδεών ο Νέος Οσιομάρτυρας», and it names him.

english.text: Contending lawfully, you threw down the enemy and were shown to be a venerable martyr, greatly renowned, of the Saviour; for you endured the cutting off of your hands and your feet, Gedeon, with patience, and therefore you deal out divine grace always to those who cry to you in faith: glory to him who gave you strength, glory to him who crowned you, glory to him who works healings for all through you.

hymns.text: Ὁσίων ἰσότιμος, καὶ Ἀθλητῶν κοινωνός, καὶ θεῖον ἀγλάϊσμα, τῆς Καρακάλλου Μονῆς, ἐδείχθης μακάριε· σὺ γὰρ στερρῶς ἀθλήσας, τὸν ἐχθρὸν ἐτροπώσω· ἔνθεν Ὁσιομάρτυς, Γεδεὼν ἐδοξάσθης, πρεσβεύων ὑπὲρ πάντων, ἡμῶν τῶν εὐφημούντων σε.

source.text: saint.gr, Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος δ’, Ταχὺ προκατάλαβε — the second of two apolytikia on the page of «Άγιος Γεδεών ο Νέος Οσιομάρτυρας», and it names him and his monastery.

english.text: You were shown, blessed one, to be of equal honour with the venerable, a partner of the contenders, and a divine adornment of the monastery of Karakallou; for contending steadfastly you routed the enemy, and from that, venerable martyr Gedeon, you were glorified, interceding for all of us who praise you.
